::: {.landing-bio}
Jacob Wallace is an Associate Professor of Public Health (Health Policy) at the Yale School of
Public Health, a Faculty Research Fellow at the National Bureau of Economic Research, and an Affiliated Professor and Scientific Advisor at the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab.

Wallace studies the economics of health insurance markets, with a focus on managed care in
public programs such as Medicaid. His research uses random assignment of people to health plans
to show what plans and their provider networks do for cost, access, and quality, and how states
can buy and pay for managed care more effectively.

His research has been published in the *American Economic Review*, the *Journal of Economic
Perspectives*, the *American Economic Journal: Applied Economics* and *Economic Policy*, and
leading medical journals, including *JAMA*, *BMJ*, and the *New England Journal of Medicine*.

Before academia, Wallace served as a Medicaid policy expert for New York State, worked as a
data scientist in Silicon Valley, and co-founded the advocacy organization Young Invincibles.
He holds degrees from Swarthmore College and Harvard University.

:::

```{r}
source("R/substack.R")
posts <- yaml::read_yaml("data/substack_posts.yml")
if (length(posts) > 0) {
  cat("## Latest writing\n\n")
  for (p in head(posts, 3)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      '<div class="post"><div class="meta">%s · %s</div><div class="headline"><a href="%s">%s</a></div></div>\n',
      html_escape(p$date), toupper(p$source), html_escape(p$url), html_escape(p$title)))
  }
  cat('\n[All writing →](writing.qmd)\n')
}
```
